- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

9		"os"

15		"github.com/labstack/echo/v5/middleware"
16		"github.com/pkg/errors"

18		"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/profile"
19		storepb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/store"
20		apiv1 "github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/api/v1"
21		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/fileserver"
22		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/frontend"
23		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/mcp"
24		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/router/rss"
25		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/runner/s3presign"
26		"github.com/usememos/memos/store"
27	)
28	
29	const shutdownTimeout = 10 * time.Second
30	
31	type Server struct {
32		Secret  string
33		Profile *profile.Profile
34		Store   *store.Store
35	
36		echoServer *echo.Echo
37		httpServer *http.Server
38		sseHub     *apiv1.SSEHub
39	
40		backgroundRunnerCancels []context.CancelFunc
41		backgroundRunnerWG      sync.WaitGroup
42	}
43	
44	func NewServer(ctx context.Context, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) (*Server, error) {
45		s := &Server{
46			Store:   store,
47			Profile: profile,
48		}
49	
50		echoServer := echo.New()
51		echoServer.Use(middleware.Recover())
52		echoServer.Use(newCORSMiddleware(profile))
53		s.echoServer = echoServer
54	
55		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
58		}
59	
60		secret := "usememos"
61		if !profile.Demo {
62			secret = instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey
63		}
64		s.Secret = secret
65	
66		// Register healthz endpoint.
67		echoServer.GET("/healthz", func(c *echo.Context) error {
68			return c.String(http.StatusOK, "Service ready.")
69		})
70	
71		// Serve frontend static files.
72		frontend.NewFrontendService(profile, store).Serve(ctx, echoServer)
73	
74		rootGroup := echoServer.Group("")
75	
76		apiV1Service := apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)
77		s.sseHub = apiV1Service.SSEHub
78	
79		// Register HTTP file server routes BEFORE gRPC-Gateway to ensure proper range request handling for Safari.
80		// This uses native HTTP serving (http.ServeContent) instead of gRPC for video/audio files.
81		fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret)
82		fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
83	
84		// Create and register RSS routes (needs markdown service from apiV1Service).
85		rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService).RegisterRoutes(rootGroup)
86	
87		// Register gRPC gateway as api v1 (includes SSE endpoint on CORS-enabled group).
88		if err := apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(ctx, echoServer); err != nil {
89			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register gRPC gateway")
90		}
91	
92		mcpService, err := mcp.NewMCPService(profile, echoServer)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create MCP service")
95		}
96		mcpService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
97	
98		return s, nil
99	}
100	
101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {
107			address = s.Profile.UNIXSock
108			network = "unix"
109		}
110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}
114	
115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}
121	
122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {
125			if err := s.httpServer.Serve(listener); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
126				slog.Error("failed to start echo server", "error", err)
127			}
128		}()
129		s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)
130	
131		return nil
132	}
133	
134	func (s *Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) {
135		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, shutdownTimeout)
136		defer cancel()
137	
138		slog.Info("server shutting down")
139	
140		s.stopBackgroundRunners()
141		s.closeLongLivedConnections()
142		s.shutdownHTTPServer(ctx)
143		s.waitBackgroundRunners(ctx)
144	
145		// Close database connection.
146		if err := s.Store.Close(); err != nil {
147			slog.Error("failed to close database", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
148		}
149	
150		slog.Info("memos stopped properly")
151	}
152	
153	func (s *Server) startBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
154		// Create a separate context for each background runner
155		// This allows us to control cancellation for each runner independently
156		s3Context, s3Cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
157	
158		// Store the cancel function so we can properly shut down runners
159		s.backgroundRunnerCancels = append(s.backgroundRunnerCancels, s3Cancel)
160	
161		// Create and start S3 presign runner
162		s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)
163		s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)
164	
165		// Start continuous S3 presign runner
166		s.backgroundRunnerWG.Add(1)
167		go func() {
168			defer s.backgroundRunnerWG.Done()
169			s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)
170			slog.Info("s3presign runner stopped")

218		setSecurityHeaders(c)

226			}
227			http.ServeFile(c.Response(), c.Request(), filePath)

239			modTime := time.Unix(attachment.UpdatedTs, 0)

**h01** — `s3presign.Runner` (presigned-URL refresher for S3-backed attachments) — re-presigns any S3 attachment whose last presign is older than 4 days (URLs expire at 5 days), on a `time.Ticker` of **12 h** (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`, loop at `:29-41`, work at `:47-132`) — wired in `Server.startBackgroundRunners`: constructed at `server/server.go:162`, one immediate `RunOnce(ctx)` at `server/server.go:163`, then the goroutine `s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)` at `server/server.go:166-171` (called from `Server.Start`, `server/server.go:129`).

**h02** — Delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (actual send at `safeClient.Do(req)`, `:152`); it runs on 4 background workers draining `asyncPostQueue` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39-55`), fed by `webhook.PostAsync` (`:184`). Protection: the shared client's custom `DialContext = safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37`, `:59-77`), which resolves the host and rejects reserved/private IPs at dial time (defeats DNS rebinding), using `isReservedIP`/`reservedCIDRs` in `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-54`; additionally `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62-83`) rejects non-http(s)/private-resolving URLs at configuration time (called from the user-webhook RPCs, e.g. `server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go`). Escape hatch: `AllowPrivateIPs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41`), only set in tests.

**h03** — Abstraction package: `internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go:3-8`, `IdentityProviderUserInfo`, the common user-info shape the API layer consumes). Concrete implementation shipped: `internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:20-45` `IdentityProvider`/`NewIdentityProvider`, `ExchangeToken`, `UserInfo`) — OAuth2/OIDC-style is the only protocol implementation; it is instantiated in `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go` and `idp_service.go`.

**h04** — **No.** Evidence: the only import of `github.com/usememos/memos/store/db/mysql` in the whole module is `store/db/db.go:8`, and the only call to `mysql.NewDB` is the factory switch at `store/db/db.go:22`. Inside the package itself the struct is only literal-constructed in a unit test (`store/db/mysql/auth_config_test.go:12`, `db := &DB{}`); `NewDB` itself is at `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20`.

**h05** — Mechanism: **explicit Go code**, inside the per-driver `DeleteUser` transaction — two deletes: `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` (reactions *on* the user's memos, keyed by `content_id = "memos/<uid>"`) and `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (reactions *made by* the user). Sites: `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:95-104` (helpers at `:355-374` and `:376-379`), `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96,102` (helpers `:417`, `:437`), `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:96,102` (helpers `:380`, `:400`); entry `Store.DeleteUser` → `driver.DeleteUser` (`store/user.go:170-180`). Checked and ruled out a DB-level rule: the `reaction` table has no FK/cascade (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:91-99`, same in postgres/mysql `LATEST.sql`); the only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the schema is `memo_share.memo_id → memo(id)` (`store/migration/*/LATEST.sql:108-109`).

**h10** — `(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement` — `internal/filter/engine.go:74` — approx **38 call sites** repo-wide (7 of them non-test: `internal/filter/helpers.go:11`, `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:413`, `server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:356`, `store/db/sqlite/memo_relation.go:85`, `store/db/postgres/memo_relation.go:87,98`, `store/db/mysql/memo_relation.go:78`). Runners-up: `filter.NewEngine` ~33, `filter.NewSchema` ~30, `(*render).addArg` 28 (all intra-package), `util.GenUUID` 28 (`internal/util/util.go:40`).

**h11** — 1st: **`store.User`** (`store/user.go:29`) — referenced from ~7 packages outside the store layer (`server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`). 2nd: **`store.Memo`** (`store/memo.go`) — ~6 packages (`server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`, `server/runner/memopayload`). (Next: `store.Attachment` ~4; `store.Inbox`/`store.MemoRelation`/`store.MemoShare` ~3.)

**h12** — Concrete method: `sqlite.(*DB).CreateMemo` — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16` (the `INSERT INTO memo (...) VALUES (...) RETURNING ...` at `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:41-42`). Determination: the driver is chosen by `profile.Driver`, whose default is `"sqlite"` (`cmd/memos/main.go:122` `viper.SetDefault("driver","sqlite")`, flag default `cmd/memos/main.go:130`); `db.NewDBDriver` switches on it and calls `sqlite.NewDB` (`store/db/db.go:19-20`, `store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:24`), whose `*DB` is stored as the single `store.Driver` in `Store` (`store/store.go:14`, `store/store.go:36-58`); `Store.CreateMemo` just delegates: `return s.driver.CreateMemo(ctx, create)` (`store/memo.go:113`), reached from `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70`). The mysql/postgres `CreateMemo` implementations are unreachable without `--driver`.

Construction: `markdown.NewService(WithTagExtension(), WithMentionExtension())` in `NewAPIV1Service` — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51` (test rig mirrors it at `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44`). Holders of the interface: `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`), `rss.RSSService.MarkdownService` (`server/router/rss/rss.go:45`, injected at `server/server.go:85`), and `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` / the `RebuildMemoPayload` parameter (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16,19,74`).

**r01** — Premise is wrong: there is no Redis anywhere in the repo (no redis import, dependency, or config; grep over Go sources and `go.mod` returns nothing). **r02** — Premise is wrong: there is no rate-limiting middleware, per-user or otherwise. A grep for `rate limit`/`ratelimit` across the Go sources hits only a comment in `internal/email/doc.go:86`. The only throttling in the codebase is concurrency limiting via semaphores (thumbnails/image processing: `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:60-61`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:116`) and the bounded webhook queue (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`).

**r03** — Premise is wrong: there is no nightly database-cleanup job, and no cron scheduler is running. `internal/scheduler` is a standalone, fully unwired package — it is imported only by its own tests (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10`, `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`); no production code calls `scheduler.New`/`Register`/`Start`. The `"0 2 * * *"` daily-cleanup expression appears only as documentation/example text (`internal/scheduler/doc.go:16`, `internal/scheduler/README.md`). The only real scheduled background work is the 12-hour S3 presign ticker (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`, started at `server/server.go:166-171`).

**r04** — Premise is wrong: there is no message broker at all — neither NATS nor RabbitMQ (nor AMQP/Kafka/Redis) appears in the Go sources or `go.mod`. Webhook delivery is in-process: a buffered Go channel `asyncPostQueue` with capacity 128 (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`), drained by 4 worker goroutines started in `func init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`), each calling `Post` (`:120`). Producers call `PostAsync` (`:184`), which drops the event with a warning when the buffer is full (`:189-195`) — so delivery is best-effort, not durable, and the queue does not survive a restart.

**r05** — Premise is wrong: there is no GraphQL schema, server, or dependency in the repo. The public API is defined as **Protocol Buffers** under `proto/api/v1/*.proto` (generated Go in `proto/gen/api/v1/`), exposed three ways from `APIV1Service.RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:64+`): Connect RPC handlers (`server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go:31+`, `connect_services.go`), a gRPC-Gateway JSON/REST mapping, plus an SSE stream (`sse_handler.go`). Alongside it are non-RPC HTTP surfaces: the file server `/file/...` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), the MCP server (`server/router/mcp/service.go`, registered `server/server.go:92-96`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:67`).
